newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST - CZECH REPUBLIC - NOV 8.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - CZECH REPUBLIC - NOV 8.

text.p: HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - The current fall in the rate of the crown on the interbank market is caused by foreign investors removing their money, according to Petr Tomek from Zivnostenska Banka.
- A definite plan for the restructuring and financing of the health-care system should be finished by the end of 1997, according to Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus.
- Water transport will require investments totalling approximately six billion crowns by the year 2005, according to a proposal prepared by the Ministry of Transport and Communications.
- Interest rates are currently at their peak and, barring any significant pressure from inflation, should decrease in the next few years, according to Daniel Heler from Credit Lyonnais Praha.
- No decisions will be made on the payment of Kreditni Banka deposit certificates during today's extraordinary general meeting of Ceska Pojistovna.
- Czechinvest processed a total of $93.5 million of direct foreign investment in the first nine months of 1996.
- Ostrava's OKD mining company is intending to raise prices on their higher quality coal by up to 15 percent.
- Receipts for Vychodoceska Plynarenska a.s. grew by 26 percent to 1,898 billion crowns in the first nine months of 1996 as compared to the same period a year earlier.

- Synthesia, a leading domestic chemical company, posted losses of 34 million crowns in the first three quarters of 1996 on turnover of 3.915 billion crowns, a decrease of 12.9 percent over the year before.

- Moravskoslezska Vagonka Studenka has resumed providing train wagons to the state after seven years. The company provided Czech railways with the first containers capable of transporting 70 tonnes of cargo at speeds of up to 120 km/hr. The company has an order worth 95 million crowns to supply 65 cargo container wagons by the end of December.

- This year's sales of computer games should reach 200 million crowns, though much depends on the upcoming Christmas season. PRAVO - Kreditni Banka's losses, officially quoted at 12 billion crowns, may actually be much lower, according to the leader of the parliamentary commission investigating the bank's collapse, Jaroslav Basta.

- Czech Railways is intending to increase fares by an average of 40 percent in 1997 according to the company's general manager, Rudolf Mladek. MLADA FRONTA DNES - Vaclav Klaus's Civic Democratic Party looks set to take the most seats in next week's senatorial elections according to a recent poll.
